title: Sweden becomes the 32nd member of NATO
body:
Sweden became the 32nd member of NATO on Thursday 7 March 2024, ending a long tradition of military neutrality. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and the foreign minister deposited Sweden's instrument of accession at the U.S. State Department in Washington, DC, with Secretary of State Antony Blinken present. The United States serves as depositary for the North Atlantic Treaty.

Sweden's entry had been delayed by objections from Turkey and Hungary. According to the report, the United States reportedly won Turkey's support by approving a sale of fighter jets, and Hungary approved Sweden's membership the same week. Blinken described the process as taking "nearly two years of tireless diplomacy" and said: "Good things come to those who wait."

Kristersson wrote on X: "Stronger together." NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said: "This is a historic day." Sweden's flag was to be raised alongside those of the other 31 allies at NATO headquarters in Brussels on 11 March and at NATO commands across Europe and North America. The report linked Sweden's change of course to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Finland, which had applied together with Sweden, had joined NATO on 4 April 2023.
